details.what_it_checks: Every campus (UNITID) that reported a year of DATA_YEARS in data/curated/dims/campus_year_sources.parquet (a release row with a count cell that is not blank, zeros included) has a site file schools/<UNITID>.json, every school file is such a campus, every school in data/curated/facts/incidents.parquet reported, and school-index.json (the site search) lists every school file once and nothing else. It compares file names only; check 2 and the per-school report compare the files' numbers.

For every site school file schools/<UNITID>.json, the yearlyTotals years are exactly the years the campus reported (campus_year_sources.parquet, zeros included) and notReported the other years of DATA_YEARS, and the total of each year (every year in the file or the aggregates; 0 when the aggregates have none) equals the sum over offenses of that school's geo "All" rows in agg_school_year_offense.parquet. The files' trends and breakdowns are not compared, and check 7 compares the aggregates with the fact table.

Of the schools with crime data in each year in agg_school_year_offense.parquet, the share that have an FTE above 0 for that year in the same file (metadata.json's enrollmentStatus names the years NCES has not published). It does not compare FTE values with the IPEDS files.

From each file's own numbers: in every rates/{window}-{code}.json file natl = natlN / natlF x 10,000 rounded half up to 2 decimals, each peer group's rate and each entry's rate = n / fteYears x 10,000 the same way (integer arithmetic), 0 <= lo <= rate <= hi, E = natlN x fteYears / natlF rounded half up to 1 decimal, and fteYearsSmaller between 1 and fteYears; every single-year rate in rates/institutions/*.json ([n, rate, lo, hi]) with its year's fte likewise. Check 12 recomputes every figure from the incidents and NCES's enrollment.

In every count ranking (one code of a rankings/*.json file's rankings, the summary codes included), entries are listed by count, largest first, ties by name (the file's campuses table), then UNITID, and each rank is 1 + the number of entries with a larger count, so tied counts share a rank (1, 2, 2, 4). In every rates/{window}-{code}.json file the entries are listed by rate (exact n / fteYears), highest first, ties by name, then base UNITID; list.n is the number of listed entries; each listed entry's position is 1 + the listed entries with a strictly higher rate and lies inside its range (rankLo-rankHi within 1-n); a state list (2+ members) the same within the state with stateN its members, and a type list (2+ members) within the peer type with typeN its members; entries not listed have no position and no listed entry is notPlaced. Check 12 recomputes the lists and ranges.

In every rankings/*.json file, totals[code] equals the sum of rankings[code]'s counts for every code, the campuses table holds every ranked campus (and the campuses ranked with 0, which check 10 checks), and the v3 rate keys (institutions, rateRankings, rateUnranked, rateNotRanked) are gone. Each rates/{window}-{code}.json file lists an institution once, summary.rated is its number of entries and stateLists and typeLists the listed entries per state and peer type, list.notPlaced the entries not placed; each entry is in rates/institutions/{id}.json, rated in that window, with the same values (natl, natl4, peerRate and peerRate4 as in the window file; the shared-site notes sharedInWith, sharedOutWith, sharedSite and coLocated as on that window's status); every rated window of an institution file is in the window files; rates/flags.json holds exactly the institution files' flags; every school file names its institution's rates file (ratesFile) exactly when it exists, and every institution file is named.

From data/curated/facts/incidents.parquet, with the rules of 04_create_aggregates.py, the count of every row of agg_school_year_offense.parquet: each year, school, offense and geography (Residence halls included), and "All" = On-campus + Non-campus + Public property (Residence halls are a subset of On-campus, so "All" leaves them out). Every row must match exactly; the totals per year and geography are shown. This proves that no count was lost, added or changed between the facts and the aggregates. It does not re-read the DOE files, so it cannot detect a value that 02_transform_to_parquet.py read wrongly from them.

Without 04's code, from data/curated/facts/incidents.parquet and dims/older_release_counts.parquet: the blocks (one campus, year and geography of On-campus, Non-campus, Public property; one cell per offense, blank = 0) counted under another campus of the same ranked state, each test needing at least 6 cells not 0, by 04's rules in order: equal blocks (same_block); equal whole campus-years, every block of the copy (whole_year); and, for a campus-year taken from an older release, whole figures or a block equal in that release to a campus whose figures now come from a newer release (whole_year_older_release, block_older_release); and the two DOE IDs of one campus (link rows of etl/reference/campus_id_changes.csv) with equal whole figures in a year both report, any number of nonzero cells: the older release's campus-year is a shadow (renumbered); last, equal whole figures of two or more institutions in one city adding up to at least 20, with fewer nonzero cells than the minimum, not already shadows (whole_year_city). Hosts are chosen by 04's order. aggs/shared_blocks.parquet must hold exactly those shadows, hosts and rules. Every rankings/*.json entry must count the school's facts without its shadow blocks (for "criminal" summed over the Criminal family, for "violent" and "property" over their offenses, for "all" over every offense), the state and national files must rank exactly the schools with such a count, and each school file's sharedFigures must list exactly its shadow blocks and their host.

dims/dim_enrollment.parquet against NCES's own figures, re-read: 2015-2020 from etl/reference/ipeds_official_fte.csv (DRVEF tables of NCES's final Access databases), 2021 on from the DRVEF CSV the pipeline reads. Every institution-year with an FTE must be there with the same FTE and percent of exclusively online students (pctdeexc), and nothing else; and its headcounts the same as NCES's raw files: total, full-time and part-time (2015-2020 the EF A file, EFALEVEL 22 + 32 and 42 + 52; 2021 on DRVEF ENRTOT, ENRFT, ENRPT) and from 2021 by level (EFUG, EFUGFT, EFGRAD, EFGRADFT, PCUDEEXC, PCGDEEXC).

Without 04's or 05's code, from the facts without shadow blocks, the reported campus-years, dim_institution, dim_enrollment's FTE and online share, NCES's raw headcounts (DRVEF 2021 on, EF A before), etl/reference/medical_campuses.csv, etl/reference/campuses_abroad.csv, etl/reference/shared_campus_overrides.csv and the raw IPEDS HD files: the campus-years that count, the institutions (base UNITIDs) each year, counts over their counting campuses in the United States (a campus DOE lists without a state, or on the reference list of campuses abroad, is counted apart), per geography (residence halls included), link campus, FTE, online share (in 2020, 2021 that of the fall ONLINE_SHARE_YEAR names when NCES has one), the two on-campus FTE estimates (proportional, and part time first, by level with the year's own share) in whole-number arithmetic, on-campus FTE = the larger rounded half up, the smaller one, uncertain when they differ by more than 5:4 or the headcounts do not add up (own, or only through a pooled institution); the rules that leave an institution-year out (HD HOSPITAL = 1, a Carnegie special-focus medical code, the reference list, a campus under two IDs, a merger family; the first one published), pooled institutions and both denominators, the Carnegie Size & Setting peer type, and the on-campus figures at listed medical-center campuses (less residence halls); the shared sites (identical on-campus copies, near-copies found again pair by pair, the reviewed override list; joined with union-find), their class, owner and roles, the rules shared_pooled and shared_campus, the pooled FTE, the campuses whose figures are in the counts and in none of the rates, the shared figures on campus and the reviewed site student figures (etl/reference/shared_site_enrollment.csv: a site-year takes its own year's figure, else the largest whose own year is at most 3 years away; derived figures upper bounds); aggs/shared_sites.parquet and aggs/near_copies.parquet. Every rankings/*.json file must list exactly its preset's counting campuses; 04's institution tables, every school file's institution years, downloads/campus-years.csv and metadata.json's rateStats.institutionYears must match, and rateStats.carnegieResearch the raw HD files' count of C21BASIC 27 institutions in the newest file with C21BASIC and of those coded 25 in the newest file with C18BASIC.

etl/reference/campus_id_changes.csv equals the campus ID-change candidates found again in data/curated/dims/campus_names.parquet (every DOE release's INSTNM, BRANCH, address and city per UNITID_P), campus_year_sources and the facts, evidence included; every row is reviewed (link or reject); each link pair is never listed in the same release, one ID is listed in the release after the other's, and they share an address or a campus name; both school files link to each other with the other ID's reported years and keep only their own years (no figures moved, no rankings changed); no other school file has idChanges; every school file is in school-index.json, titled by its DOE campus name (dim_institution campus_name) when it is not a main campus.

details.what_it_checks: Without 04's, 05's or rates.py's code, from the institution-year data (institution-years with a counting campus, their on-campus/residence-hall/non-campus/public-property counts per offense, medical-center and shared on-campus figures, NCES FTE, the rate denominator and its smaller estimate, rules, online uncertainty, peer type) and the rule constants written out in this check: each institution's status in every 3-year window without 2020 (missingYears, scope, size, excluded, rated), the window counts, FTE-years, reason (shared: a guest or participant at a shared site in a year of the window unless its reviewed site students (each site-year its own year's figure, else the largest within 3 years; sharedSite.figures gives each campus's name, each figure's own year and whether derived; upperBound when any figure is an upper bound) are at most 1/10 of its FTE-years, then verdicts withheld; online; medical_campus: medical share at least 1/4) and the shared-site notes (sharedInWith, sharedOutWith, sharedSite, coLocated), the unresolved-hospital note (hospitalUnresolved {name, years} from etl/reference/hospital_unresolved.csv, read here, and the institution file's full row), the national and peer rates as exact fractions (2 and 4 decimals), phi with the ramp, raised to T s^2 / N when the window's yearly counts spread more (s^2 their sample variance; phiFrom), the gamma interval (own incomplete gamma, bisection), rate/lo/hi/lo4/hi4/E rounded half up, the verdicts against the exact reference (online: both FTE estimates must agree), the unusual-year flags (negative binomial tail < 0.001) and the verdict without the flagged excess (the yearly counts less each flagged year's excess, their spread), the ordered lists (E >= 20 exactly; an on-campus unusual-year flag of the code in the window: not placed; exact order, positions, pairwise z with each member's variance the larger of the model's and T s^2 and Bonferroni critical values from an own normal quantile, ranges widened to the position, state and type lists from 2 members, composition), every window file's header (compositionShare, typeLists) and summary, rates/institutions (single-year T = 1 entries and notRated reasons, window statuses, absentYears: each data year without an institution-year, either no campus of it reported that year or each campus that did has only shadow blocks, whose host campuses and institutions it names, found from the reported campus-years and shadow blocks; every missing year of a missingYears window has one), rates/flags.json, the count flag (3 x P99, numpy linear percentile, count >= 20) in every rankings file, school files' ratesFile/rated/notRated/flags, metadata.json rateRules and rateStats, config.py's constants, the design's test vectors, A4 (no placed entry has a flag, every notPlaced one has one) and A5 (the model's bounds rise with N).

A1: single-year leave-one-out predictive coverage of on-campus counts under the published dispersion (c per code, ramp, and the other years' own spread when larger), observed against expected from 600 panels simulated from the model and judged by the same rule (PCG64 seed 11, fresh per code and period); tolerance 0.02 either way over units with a mean >= 2/year; in bands with >= 100 units, fails when observed is below expected by more than 0.03 (intervals too narrow: verdicts overstate certainty) or above it by more than 0.05 (intervals too wide: fewer verdicts, the safer error). The 20+ band of violent, criminal_xmvt, burglary, rape is tested whatever its size, each limit widened below 100 units by 2 binomial standard errors of the expected share over its unit-years. Every band is listed in rows; tested is false when not tested.

A3: non-main campuses whose DOE branch name + address match MEDICAL_SCREEN_PATTERN, in an institution-year with a single-year rate, with sum over criminal_xmvt offenses of max(0, on campus - residence halls) >= 5 and >= 1/10 of the institution's on-campus criminal_xmvt count, not covered for that year by medical_campuses.csv or medical_campus_reviews.csv.

schools.what_it_checks: Per site school file: yearlyTotals equal the aggregates' geo "All" totals (as check 2), and fteByYear and fte equal dim_enrollment's FTE for the school's years (FAIL otherwise); WARNING when fewer than 80% of its years have an FTE. A school that fails makes the overall status FAIL.
